outcome: Transferral to neonatal intensive care ward
Third stage of labor complications (postpartum hemorrhage, need for manual placental removal or curettage)
Recurrence of iSUA in subsequent pregnancy
Recurrence of anomalous cord or placenta characteristics in subsequent pregnancy
cohort: The study included 918,933 singleton pregnancies with gestational age >16 weeks at birth from the Medical Birth Registry of Norway between 1999 and 2014.
finding: The presence of isolated single umbilical artery (iSUA) was associated with a more than five times increased risk of intrauterine and perinatal death, as well as increased risks of preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age neonate, and various placental and cord complications including third stage of labor complications.
gest_age: >16 weeks at birth (inclusion criteria); preterm birth and small-for-gestational-age as outcomes
